## File: `references/languages/javascript.md`

### Language Guidance — JavaScript/TypeScript

Load `../standards/google-typescript-style.md` (GTS-01…GTS-23). Its elements are scored under CS-05, CS-04 (GTS-22)
and SQ-06 (GTS-20, GTS-21). Apply "TS" rows to `.ts`/`.tsx` files only. A documented convention (`eslint.config.*`,
`.eslintrc*`, `.prettierrc*`, `biome.json`, `tsconfig.json` `strict`/`noImplicitAny`, `.editorconfig`) prevails over
the guide's defaults. Ignored caught errors on security-relevant paths belong to review-security-operational SEC-OP-02.

Signals:
- Formatter/linter config counts as "formatting enforced" for CS-02: `.prettierrc*`, `prettier` key in `package.json`,
  `eslint.config.*`/`.eslintrc*`, `biome.json`, `dprint.json`.
- Static checking adopted (SQR-36): `tsconfig.json` with `"strict": true` or `"noImplicitAny": true`; inconsistent use
  is widespread `any`, `// @ts-ignore` or `!` assertions in files under that config.
- Project references for dependency-cycle checks: `tsconfig.json` `references`, workspace `package.json`
  (`workspaces`), `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `nx.json`, `turbo.json`.

## File: `references/standards/google-typescript-style.md`

*Load rule: GTS-01…GTS-23. Load only if JavaScript/TypeScript is detected.*

### Google TypeScript Style Guide — localized summary

- Level: informational only; severity is the owning check's default.
- **Load only when language `javascript` is detected.** Apply "TS" rows to `.ts`/`.tsx` files only; "TS/JS" rows also
  to `.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`/`.jsx` files. A documented team convention (ESLint/Prettier/Biome config, `.editorconfig`,
  `tsconfig.json` settings, a written style guide) prevails over these defaults (SKILL.md), e.g. a Prettier config with
  double quotes passes GTS-11. Generated code is exempt (`#generated-code-mostly-exempt`). `@deprecated` marking is
  judged by `review-maintainability` MAINT-05, not here.

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| GTS-01 | Types, classes, interfaces, enums and decorators use UpperCamelCase; variables, parameters, functions, methods and properties use lowerCamelCase; module-level constants and enum values may use CONSTANT_CASE. | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-02 | Names are descriptive; acronyms are treated as words (`loadHttpUrl`); no `opt_` prefixes and no leading or trailing underscores. | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-03 | Variables are declared with `const` by default and `let` when reassigned; `var` is never used; one variable per declaration. | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-04 | Modules use named exports, not default exports. | TS/JS modules | CS-05 |
| GTS-05 | ES modules are used: no `namespace`, no `require` imports in TypeScript, no `/// <reference>` directives. | TS | CS-05 |
| GTS-06 | Equality uses `===`/`!==` (except `== null` to cover both null and undefined). | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-07 | `any` is avoided; `unknown` or a specific type is used instead. | TS | CS-05 |
| GTS-08 | Type and non-null (`!`) assertions are used only with a stated reason; runtime checks are preferred; assertions use `as`, not angle brackets. | TS | CS-05 |
| GTS-09 | `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error` (outside tests) and `@ts-nocheck` aren't used; all files pass type checking. | TS | CS-05 |
| GTS-10 | Type aliases don't include `\|null`/`\|undefined`; optional fields and parameters use `?`. | TS | CS-05 |
| GTS-11 | String literals use single quotes; statements end with explicit semicolons (no reliance on automatic semicolon insertion). | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-12 | Control statements always use braced blocks; every `switch` has a `default` case, placed last. | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-13 | `for…in` isn't used on arrays; object iteration filters own properties or uses `Object.keys`/`entries`. | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-14 | No `eval` or `Function(string)`, no `with`, no `debugger` in production code, no wrapper objects (`new String`), no `Array()` constructor, no modification of built-in prototypes. | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-15 | Class members don't use the `public` modifier (except non-readonly parameter properties) or `#private` fields; parameter properties are preferred over manual assignment. | TS classes | CS-05 |
| GTS-16 | Getters are pure (no observable side effects); accessors aren't created with `Object.defineProperty`. | TS/JS classes | CS-05 |
| GTS-17 | Named functions use function declarations; function expressions are replaced by arrow functions; `this` is used only in class members or explicitly typed functions. | TS/JS | CS-05 |
| GTS-18 | `const enum` isn't used, and enum values aren't coerced to booleans. | TS enums | CS-05 |
| GTS-19 | Simple array types use `T[]`, complex ones `Array<T>`; interfaces are preferred over object type-literal aliases. | TS | CS-05 |
| GTS-20 | Only `Error` objects (or subclasses) are thrown or used as promise rejection reasons, created with `new`. | TS/JS | SQ-06 |
| GTS-21 | An empty `catch` block has a comment explaining why ignoring the error is correct. | TS/JS | SQ-06 |
| GTS-22 | All top-level exports have JSDoc that adds information beyond the name; JSDoc doesn't repeat types already in the TypeScript signature. | TS/JS exported API | CS-04 |
| GTS-23 | New code follows the file's and directory's established style when the guide is silent; new files use the guide (or the team convention). | TS/JS | CS-05 |
